item.name: Cinderhack
item.entry:
Officially registered as steam hackney carriages, these three-wheeled taxis are universally known as Cinderhacks. They are the most common form of hired transportation in {{FOGPORT}}, crowding the streets around tram stations, markets, docks, hotels, and public buildings.

A Cinderhack has one wooden steering wheel at the front, two larger driving wheels behind, a narrow driver’s perch, and a covered bench for two or three passengers. A compact boiler mounted behind the passenger compartment drives the rear axle by chain or piston. Most are noisy, soot-streaked, and assembled from parts belonging to several previous cabs.

Many Cinderhacks are operated by {{THRALLO}} drivers, whose strength, patience, and ability to see through the fog make them particularly suited to the trade.

The End of Horses

Before the {{CATASTROPHE}}, Fogport depended upon horses. Thousands hauled freight, drew private carriages, carried constables, and pulled trams through the city.

During the Catastrophe, the horses did not simply die.

They changed.

Stable doors burst open throughout Fogport as the animals reared onto two legs and became the first of the monstrous {{HORSEMEN}}. Some tore away their harnesses. Others could not; leather, brass, blinders, and carriage fittings had already become part of them. They killed grooms, trampled passengers, and fled into the fog in violent herds.

No true horses remain in Fogport. Horsemen are occasionally sighted beyond the walls or heard galloping upright through abandoned streets, but they cannot be domesticated and react murderously to bridles, saddles, and the smell of a stable.

Old equestrian statues are considered unlucky. Most have been removed, altered, or quietly given human feet.

Rise of the Cinderhack

With every horse gone, the city faced starvation. Food, coal, cargo, and people could no longer move through the streets in sufficient numbers. Steam vehicles had existed before the Catastrophe, but only as expensive curiosities prone to breakdown and explosion.

Necessity made them ordinary.

The first Cinderhacks were improvised from broken carriages, industrial pumps, laundry boilers, and salvaged tram components. Their three-wheel construction was cheap, maneuverable, and narrow enough for Fogport’s crooked streets. Within a decade, they had replaced horse-drawn cabs almost completely.

Modern Cinderhacks are still built more like appliances than automobiles. Every district has mechanics capable of repairing one with stove parts, plumbing fittings, and sufficient profanity.

Hiring a Cinderhack

Licensed Cinderhacks display a numbered brass plaque beneath the canopy. Cab ranks are marked by iron water pumps and coke bins where drivers refill their boilers while waiting for fares.

To summon one, a passenger raises a hand and shouts, “Hack!” Striking a match in the fog is also customary, though this occasionally summons things other than taxis.

Fares depend upon distance, district, weather, passenger weight, luggage, and whether the driver believes the destination is haunted. Travel into {{SHAMBLES}} generally costs double. Travel out costs whatever the driver demands after arriving.

A prudent passenger settles the fare before boarding.

Reputation

Cinderhacks are loud, smoky, uncomfortable, and only slightly less dangerous than the streets they travel. Their boilers rupture. Their brakes fail. Their drivers take shortcuts through alleys omitted from every reputable map.

Nevertheless, they are dependable by Fogport standards.

When the fog is thick and something is following, the hiss of a Cinderhack boiler may be the finest sound in the world.
